name: cosmic-mint

source.origin: user-provided conversation Image #1, recovered from the matching local Codex clipboard cache

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided annotated review screenshot and written clarification
reviewEvidence.note: The red rectangle marks a meteor trail; the annotation itself and capture UI are excluded from the theme.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided third-round annotated review screenshot; the same PNG was uploaded twice
reviewEvidence.note: Confirms solid side-stage fills still read as blank bars, fixed paired meteor cycles and paths feel artificial, and grouped star opacity changes are not visibly perceived as twinkling.
Rejects two-column cards that stretch to fill the remaining slide height when their text content is short.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided fourth-round browser screenshot with trajectory annotations
reviewEvidence.note: Freezes the meteor region above the main diagonal: enter through the left edge, travel smoothly toward the upper right, exit through the top edge, and move more slowly than 0.1.4. It also records unreliable repeated trackpad gestures.
Explicitly rejects cross-shaped stars with horizontal and vertical rays; all primary stars must remain circular dots.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided close reference for the dotted Earth, Americas-facing frame
reviewEvidence.note: Confirms tiny dots are restricted to land, with dark unfilled oceans and a restrained blue rim.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided close reference for the dotted Earth, Africa-facing frame
reviewEvidence.note: Confirms continent silhouettes move through a circular globe window while oceans remain visually empty.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided close reference for the dotted Earth, alternate Americas-facing frame
reviewEvidence.note: Confirms the rotation is slow and the land-dot texture stays fine and low contrast.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided close reference for the galaxy background
reviewEvidence.note: Confirms a natural granular diagonal Milky Way band rather than a smooth gradient color block.

reviewEvidence.origin: user-provided close reference for meteor styling
reviewEvidence.note: Confirms two thin staggered pale trails and supports a slightly faster crossing speed.

canvas.fact: The captured frame is 2118 × 1112 and contains a widescreen presentation inside a live-stream capture.
canvas.treatment: Use the project 16:9 canvas; do not reproduce live-stream chrome.

palette.evidence: Near-black blue dominates the sampled frame.
The code panel is a slightly lighter indigo surface.
Primary explanatory copy is cool white.
Secondary details use a cool blue gray.
The main title uses a luminous mint cyan.
Low-contrast violet-blue light appears in the background.
The main panel uses a thin cool-indigo outline.

typography.fact: Large bold sans-serif display type, smaller bold sans-serif subheading, and monospaced instructional content form three clear levels.
typography.scale: Display is roughly 2.2–2.6 times body size; body uses generous line spacing.
typography.alignment: All presentation content is left aligned.
typography.fallback: System sans-serif and system monospace only; the exact source font is unknown.

spacing.fact: The layout uses a broad left margin, a compact vertical title stack, then a single wide content panel.
spacing.system: 8px base unit, 72px safe area, 24px grid gap, and 24–32px component padding.

geometry.fact: The primary container is a wide low-contrast rectangle with a fine outline and restrained corner radius.
geometry.treatment: Use 8–14px radii, 1px borders, and no heavy card shadows.

layoutGrammar.fact: One dominant title, one explanatory line, and one main information region create a top-to-bottom reading path.
layoutGrammar.density: Medium-low outside the main panel and medium inside it.
layoutGrammar.extension: Other layouts retain a single dominant composition rather than dashboard-like card collections.

imageTreatment.fact: No content photograph is used; the background is structured by a granular diagonal galaxy haze, layered stars, glow, and a partial Earth whose land alone is rendered with tiny dots.
imageTreatment.extension: Use CSS gradients and restrained translucent overlays; supplied images receive a cool, slightly saturated treatment.

graphicLanguage.fact: Layered stars, a natural diagonal Milky Way band, cyan-violet glow, and a large off-canvas Earth with continent-only dots provide recognisable depth without competing with text.
graphicLanguage.extension: Rebuild the atmosphere with deterministic local SVG textures and CSS pseudo-elements; do not copy the source artwork.

motion.fact: The user supplied three Earth frames that confirm slow rotation, a meteor reference showing thin staggered trails, a third-round review rejecting fixed meteor waves, and a fourth-round review that freezes left-edge-to-top-edge meteor geometry, slower travel, circular stars, and reliable gesture navigation.
motion.treatment: Use a 48-second continuous continent-strip drift; fifteen circular stars with independent twinkle peaks, glows, delays, and 4–12px firefly-like drift; and session-seeded irregular waves of one to three smooth meteors that enter through the left edge, remain in the upper half above the main diagonal, and leave through the top edge over 1.9–2.6 seconds. Extend the same galaxy and sparse-light language across non-16:9 stage margins. Freeze or omit transient motion for print, render mode, and reduced-motion users.
motion.fallback: The static frame must show a readable continent-only dotted Earth and sparse stars without depending on a captured random meteor state.

chartStyle.fact: The reference does not show a chart.
chartStyle.extension: Use mint as the primary series, cool violet and cyan as secondary series, dark tracks, and direct labels.

inferences.rationale: The captured image includes stream UI and is not itself the clean slide boundary.

inferences.decision: Rebuild the star field and diagonal granular galaxy as deterministic local SVG texture plus restrained CSS layers instead of embedding the source background.
inferences.rationale: The reusable system is the depth, grain, and light hierarchy, not the proprietary raster texture or a smooth gradient block.

inferences.decision: Animate a code-native dotted world strip through a shaded circular globe window; only continent paths receive dots and ocean areas remain unpatterned.
inferences.rationale: The three supplied frames explicitly reject a uniform full-sphere dot matrix and confirm slow land movement across a dark ocean.

inferences.decision: Generate irregular waves of one to three thin luminous trails using a crypto-seeded per-session PRNG; each trail enters through the left edge, crosses the upper half above the main diagonal, and leaves through the top edge over 1.9–2.6 seconds while staying left of the Earth.
inferences.rationale: The fourth-round annotation explicitly freezes the start and exit edges, desired upper-half region, and slower speed while retaining varied smooth trajectories.

inferences.decision: Use outlined translucent surfaces for metrics, comparisons, timelines, and charts.
inferences.rationale: Only a single code panel is visible, so multi-layout component behavior is a design extension.

inferences.decision: Apply a cool contrast and saturation filter to content images.
inferences.rationale: No content image appears in the reference; the choice follows the observed cool luminous palette.

unresolved.reason: The raster reference cannot prove the exact font family.
No chart or data visualization is visible.
No content photograph or crop behavior is visible.
The reference only demonstrates a dark presentation.
The user requires one to three meteors per wave with irregular timing but leaves the exact probability distribution to implementation and visual review.

forbidden: copying the reference raster background into the theme
uniform dots covering the full globe including oceans
a smooth diagonal gradient used as a substitute for granular galaxy texture
reproducing live-stream comments, controls, counts, or platform branding
remote fonts or remote image URLs
rainbow gradients or neon colors outside the mint-cyan-violet system
theme selectors tied to slide ids or document-specific copy

initialReview.note: Final acceptance remains subject to user review against the original reference.

revisionHistory.reason: The Earth used uniform full-sphere dots, the galaxy read as a color block, and the meteor treatment did not match the paired thin trails.
The user accepted the continent-only dotted Earth, granular Milky Way texture, and paired meteor treatment before requesting a later player and motion refinement.
The solid side stage still read as blank bars, the fixed paired meteor period and path felt artificial, and grouped star animation did not produce visible twinkling.

Two-column cards still stretched vertically, meteors crossed the middle too quickly instead of entering from the left and leaving through the top, some stars rendered as crosses, and the fixed wheel cooldown swallowed subsequent trackpad gestures.
The user accepted the final Goal 003 delivery after G11 fixed repeated same-direction trackpad gestures while retaining content-sized cards, circular stars, and 1.9–2.6-second upper-half meteors.

revisionReview.note: The user verified and accepted the final 0.1.5 visual system and Goal 003 G11 navigation behavior on 2026-09-02.
